summary: @servicetitan/install preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes heavily obfuscated 727KB payload
details: @servicetitan/install@38.1.4 declares a `preinstall` script (`node setup.mjs`) that at npm install time downloads the Bun runtime from oven-sh GitHub releases and uses it to execFileSync a sibling file `math_init.js` — a 727KB heavily obfuscated bundle (rotating string-array, char-code decoder, `with`-statement parser-evasion tricks, `_0x...` renamed identifiers). `setup.mjs` itself is also obfuscated with the same style (packed string-map objects wrapping every http/execFileSync call). Both `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` sit at the tarball root but are NOT listed in the package.json `files` manifest (which declares only `bin`, `dist`, `src`), so the two files that actually run at install were shipped outside the author's declared publish manifest. Using an alternate runtime (Bun) to execute an obfuscated payload evades Node-based install-time scanners, and the payload's name (`math_init.js`) has no relation to the package's advertised installer-wrapper purpose. The shape matches an unauthorized modification to the published artifact for the @servicetitan scope: an alternate-runtime dropper executing an obfuscated blob at install time, with manifest/tarball mismatch consistent with a scope compromise.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
